biography: Joey van Splunteren, a name quickly gaining traction in the open-wheel circuit, hails from the small Dutch town of Zandvoort, practically within earshot of the legendary Circuit Zandvoort. Growing up, the roar of engines was the soundtrack to his life, and he spent countless hours mimicking racing lines on his bicycle around the neighborhood, often earning the ire of local residents. His actual racing career began somewhat late, at age 18, after winning a local karting competition sponsored by a cheese factory (a fact he tries to downplay these days). Lacking the deep pockets of many of his rivals, Joey clawed his way up through the Formula Trainer series, showcasing an undeniable raw talent, even if occasionally marred by impulsive decisions. After a strong showing in Formula Trainer Advance, including a stunning last-lap overtake at Spa, he's now on the cusp of breaking into a higher tier, but needs to prove his consistency to secure a coveted seat. His flashy persona both attracts fans and rubs some the wrong way, but one thing is certain: Joey van Splunteren is never boring.
drivingStyle: Joey’s driving style is best described as aggressive and opportunistic. He is known for his daring late-braking maneuvers and his willingness to push the car to its absolute limit, often flirting with disaster. While undeniably quick, this approach can lead to inconsistent results, with spectacular wins often followed by costly crashes. He has a knack for tire management, often nursing his rubber through long stints, only to unleash a blistering pace in the final laps. He thrives under pressure, often performing his best when the stakes are highest.

rivalries.reason: A clash of egos and contrasting driving styles. Ricardo, known for his calculated precision, frequently criticizes Joey's reckless abandon, leading to heated exchanges both on and off the track.
A rivalry born from several on-track collisions, most notably at Monza in Formula Trainer Advance, where Joey's aggressive move resulted in both drivers retiring from the race.
A close championship battle in Formula Trainer, where Isabelle ultimately edged out Joey for the title. Joey has been determined to prove he's the superior driver ever since.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky orange socks, gifted to him by his grandmother.
Listens to Dutch hardcore techno music exactly 30 minutes before every race.
Refuses to eat anything containing tomatoes on race days, claiming it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: "I don't race to finish second. Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the Spa-Francorchamps round in Formula Trainer Advance with a stunning last-lap overtake, proving his ability to perform under pressure and solidifying his reputation as a rising star.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the Formula Trainer championship decider at Hockenheim after a misjudgment in wet conditions, costing him the title and a guaranteed step up to the next series.
